source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sender, calling, recipients, and regional scope.
verses.before: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, To the church of God that is in Corinth, together with all the holy ones who are in the whole of Achaia:
verses.after: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and Timothy our brother, to God's church in Corinth, together with all the saints throughout Achaia:
verses.tsw_comparator: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, To the church of God that is in Corinth, together with all the holy ones who are in the whole of Achaia:

verses.rationale: Retains the paired greeting and both sources.
verses.before: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.after: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps the blessing and repeated relational titles.
verses.before: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort,
verses.after: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and God of all comfort.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort,

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated comfort language and its purpose.
verses.before: who comforts us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to comfort people who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
verses.after: He comforts us in all our affliction so that we can comfort those in any affliction with the comfort we ourselves receive from God.
verses.tsw_comparator: who comforts us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired overflowing of suffering and comfort.
verses.before: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.
verses.after: For just as Christ's sufferings overflow to us, so through Christ our comfort also overflows.
verses.tsw_comparator: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.

verses.rationale: Preserves both conditions and endurance amid the same harms.
verses.before: But if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; and if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which is at work in patient endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer.
verses.after: If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which takes effect as you patiently endure the same sufferings we also suffer.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; and if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which is at work in patient endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer.

verses.rationale: Keeps shared suffering and comfort in parallel.
verses.before: And our hope for you is firm, knowing that as you are partners in the sufferings, so also you are partners in the comfort.
verses.after: Our hope for you is firm, because we know that as you share in the sufferings, so you also share in the comfort.
verses.tsw_comparator: And our hope for you is firm, knowing that as you are partners in the sufferings, so also you are partners in the comfort.

verses.rationale: Names the actual severity and Asia without softening despair.
verses.before: For we do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, about the affliction that came to us in Asia, that we were weighed down beyond measure, beyond our strength, so that we despaired even of life.
verses.after: Brothers and sisters, we do not want you to be unaware of the affliction we experienced in Asia. We were burdened far beyond our strength, so much that we despaired even of living.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, about the affliction that came to us in Asia, that we were weighed down beyond measure, beyond our strength, so that we despaired even of life.

verses.rationale: Keeps the inward verdict, purpose, and resurrection ground.
verses.before: Indeed, we ourselves had the sentence of death within ourselves, so that we might not trust in ourselves but in God who raises the dead,
verses.after: Indeed, we felt within ourselves that we had received a sentence of death. This happened so that we would not trust in ourselves but in God, who raises the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, we ourselves had the sentence of death within ourselves, so that we might not trust in ourselves but in God who raises the dead,

verses.rationale: Preserves past, future, and continuing hope.
verses.before: who rescued us from so great a death and will rescue us, in whom we have set our hope that he will rescue us again,
verses.after: He rescued us from such great danger of death and will rescue us. We have set our hope on him that he will rescue us again,
verses.tsw_comparator: who rescued us from so great a death and will rescue us, in whom we have set our hope that he will rescue us again,

verses.rationale: Keeps the community's prayer and many-person thanksgiving.
verses.before: as you also help us by prayer, so that thanks may be given by many on our behalf for the gift granted to us through many.
verses.after: as you also help us by your prayer, so that many may give thanks on our behalf for the gracious gift given to us through the prayers of many.
verses.tsw_comparator: as you also help us by prayer, so that thanks may be given by many on our behalf for the gift granted to us through many.

verses.rationale: Preserves conscience, conduct, contrast, and the marked focus on Corinth.
verses.before: For our boast is this: the testimony of our conscience, that we conducted ourselves in the world with holiness and sincerity from God, not by fleshly wisdom but by the grace of God, and especially toward you.
verses.after: For this is our reason for boasting: the testimony of our conscience that we conducted ourselves in the world—and especially toward you—with God's holiness and sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom but with God's grace.
verses.tsw_comparator: For our boast is this: the testimony of our conscience, that we conducted ourselves in the world with holiness and sincerity from God, not by fleshly wisdom but by the grace of God, and especially toward you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the wordplay between reading and recognizing in natural English.
verses.before: For we write to you nothing other than what you can read and also understand; and I hope that you will understand fully,
verses.after: For we are not writing you anything other than what you can read and understand. I hope you will understand fully,
verses.tsw_comparator: For we write to you nothing other than what you can read and also understand; and I hope that you will understand fully,

verses.rationale: Retains partial recognition and reciprocal boasting at the day.
verses.before: just as you have understood us in part, that we are your boast, as you also are ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus.
verses.after: just as you have understood us in part, that on the day of our Lord Jesus we are your reason for boasting, just as you are ours.
verses.tsw_comparator: just as you have understood us in part, that we are your boast, as you also are ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's plan and the second benefit.
verses.before: And in this confidence I intended first to come to you, so that you might have a second grace,
verses.after: Because I was confident of this, I intended to come to you first, so that you might receive grace a second time.
verses.tsw_comparator: And in this confidence I intended first to come to you, so that you might have a second grace,

verses.rationale: Preserves the planned route and the Corinthians' support.
verses.before: and through you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come back to you, and by you to be sent on my way to Judea.
verses.after: I intended to travel through you to Macedonia, then come back to you from Macedonia and have you send me on my way to Judea.
verses.tsw_comparator: and through you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come back to you, and by you to be sent on my way to Judea.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical questions and doubled yes/no.
verses.before: So, when I intended this, did I act with fickleness? Or what I plan, do I plan according to the flesh, so that with me it is “Yes, yes” and “No, no”?
verses.after: When I intended this, was I being fickle? Or do I make my plans according to the flesh, so that with me it is both “Yes, yes” and “No, no”?
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, when I intended this, did I act with fickleness? Or what I plan, do I plan according to the flesh, so that with me it is “Yes, yes” and “No, no”?

verses.rationale: Grounds the denial in God's faithfulness.
verses.before: But as God is faithful, our word to you is not “Yes” and “No.”
verses.after: But as God is faithful, our word to you is not both “Yes” and “No.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But as God is faithful, our word to you is not “Yes” and “No.”

verses.rationale: Retains all preachers and the contrast centered in Christ.
verses.before: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we proclaimed among you—Silvanus and Timothy and I—was not “Yes” and “No,” but in him it has always been “Yes.”
verses.after: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we proclaimed among you—through me, Silvanus, and Timothy—did not become “Yes” and “No,” but in him it has become “Yes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we proclaimed among you—Silvanus and Timothy and I—was not “Yes” and “No,” but in him it has always been “Yes.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the promise fulfillment and the community's response.
verses.before: For as many as are the promises of God, in him they are “Yes.” Therefore through him also the “Amen” is spoken by us to the glory of God.
verses.after: For however many God's promises are, in him they are “Yes.” Therefore through him we also say the “Amen” to God for his glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as many as are the promises of God, in him they are “Yes.” Therefore through him also the “Amen” is spoken by us to the glory of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves God's action on both workers and readers.
verses.before: But the one who establishes us with you in Christ and anointed us is God,
verses.after: The one who establishes us with you in Christ and anointed us is God.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the one who establishes us with you in Christ and anointed us is God,

verses.rationale: Keeps seal, Spirit, heart, and commercial image.
verses.before: who also sealed us and gave the Spirit in our hearts as a first pledge.
verses.after: He also sealed us and gave the Spirit in our hearts as a down payment.
verses.tsw_comparator: who also sealed us and gave the Spirit in our hearts as a first pledge.

verses.rationale: Retains the solemn oath and stated motive.
verses.before: Yet I call God as witness against my soul, that it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.
verses.after: But I call God as witness against my own life: it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I call God as witness against my soul, that it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.

verses.rationale: Preserves the denial of domination and collaborative contrast.
verses.before: Not that we lord it over your trust, but we are coworkers for your joy, for you stand firm in the faith.
verses.after: Not that we rule over your faith; rather, we work with you for your joy, because you stand firm by faith.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not that we lord it over your faith, but we are coworkers for your joy, for you stand firm in the faith.

verses.rationale: Keeps the personal decision and relational setting.
verses.before: For I decided this for myself, not to come to you again in sorrow.
verses.after: So I decided this for myself: I would not come to you again in sorrow.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I decided this for myself, not to come to you again in sorrow.

verses.rationale: Preserves the pointed reciprocal question.
verses.before: For if I cause you sorrow, who then is there to make me glad but the one whom I have made sorrowful?
verses.after: For if I cause you sorrow, who is left to make me glad except the one I have caused sorrow?
verses.tsw_comparator: For if I cause you sorrow, who then is there to make me glad but the one whom I have made sorrowful?

verses.rationale: Keeps the purpose and shared joy.
verses.before: I wrote as I did, so that when I came I might not have sorrow from people who ought to make me glad, because I am confident about all of you, that my joy is the joy of all of you.
verses.after: I wrote as I did so that when I came I would not be grieved by those who should have made me glad. I was confident about all of you, that my joy belongs to all of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I wrote as I did, so that when I came I might not have sorrow from those who ought to make me glad, because I am confident about all of you, that my joy is the joy of all of you.

verses.rationale: Retains distress, tears, denied aim, and love.
verses.before: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears—not so that you might be grieved, but so that you might know the love that I have abundantly for you.
verses.after: For I wrote to you through much affliction and anguish of heart, with many tears—not to cause you sorrow, but so that you might know the abundant love I have especially for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears—not so that you might be grieved, but so that you might know the love that I have abundantly for you.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's qualification rather than universalizing the harm.
verses.before: But if someone has caused sorrow, he has caused it not to me alone, but in some measure—not to overstate it—to all of you.
verses.after: But if anyone has caused sorrow, he has not caused sorrow to me alone, but—to avoid overstating it—to some extent to all of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if anyone has caused sorrow, he has caused it not to me alone, but in some measure—not to overstate it—to all of you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the communal action and its sufficiency.
verses.before: This punishment by the majority is enough for such a one,
verses.after: The punishment imposed by the majority is enough for such a person.
verses.tsw_comparator: This punishment by the majority is enough for such a one,

verses.rationale: Keeps the reversal and danger of engulfing grief.
verses.before: so that on the contrary you should rather forgive and comfort him, lest he be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
verses.after: So now, instead, you should forgive and comfort him, so that he is not overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that on the contrary you should rather forgive and comfort him, lest he be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.

verses.rationale: States the requested public confirmation.
verses.before: So I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
verses.after: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the stated test and its scope.
verses.before: For this is why I wrote, so that I might test you and know whether you are obedient in everything.
verses.after: This is also why I wrote: to learn by testing whether you are obedient in everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is why I wrote, so that I might test you and know whether you are obedient in everything.

verses.rationale: Keeps the conditional qualification and Christward setting.
verses.before: Anyone whom you forgive, I also forgive. Indeed, what I have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, has been for your sake in the presence of Christ,
verses.after: Anyone you forgive, I also forgive. Indeed, whatever I have forgiven—if I had anything to forgive—I have forgiven for your sake in the presence of Christ,
verses.tsw_comparator: Anyone whom you forgive, I also forgive. Indeed, what I have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, has been for your sake in the presence of Christ,

verses.rationale: Preserves purpose and awareness of designs.
verses.before: so that we may not be outwitted by Satan, for we are not unaware of his designs.
verses.after: so that Satan might not take advantage of us, for we are not unaware of his schemes.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that we may not be outwitted by Satan, for we are not unaware of his designs.

verses.rationale: Keeps place, mission, and opened-door image.
verses.before: When I came to Troas to proclaim the good news of Christ, even though a door was opened for me in the Lord,
verses.after: When I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ and a door was opened for me in the Lord,
verses.tsw_comparator: When I came to Troas to proclaim the good news of Christ, even though a door was opened for me in the Lord,

verses.rationale: Preserves inner unrest, kinship, farewell, and movement.
verses.before: my spirit had no rest because I did not find my brother Titus there; so I took leave of them and went on to Macedonia.
verses.after: I had no relief in my spirit because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.
verses.tsw_comparator: my spirit had no rest because I did not find my brother Titus there; so I took leave of them and went on to Macedonia.

verses.rationale: Keeps the potentially captive triumph image and fragrance metaphor.
verses.before: But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ and manifests through us the fragrance of the knowledge of him in every place.
verses.after: But thanks be to God, who always leads us in Christ's triumphal procession and through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of knowing him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ and manifests through us the fragrance of the knowledge of him in every place.

verses.rationale: Retains audience groups and Godward fragrance.
verses.before: For we are the aroma of Christ to God among people who are being saved and among people who are perishing—
verses.after: For to God we are Christ's fragrance among those being saved and among those perishing:
verses.tsw_comparator: For we are the aroma of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing—

verses.rationale: Keeps the stark double outcome and closing question.
verses.before: to the one a fragrance from death to death, to the other a fragrance from life to life. And who is sufficient for these things?
verses.after: to some, an aroma from death leading to death; to others, an aroma from life leading to life. And who is sufficient for these things?
verses.tsw_comparator: to the one a fragrance from death to death, to the other a fragrance from life to life. And who is sufficient for these things?

verses.rationale: Preserves commercial accusation, sincerity, source, and accountability.
verses.before: For we are not like so many, peddling the word of God; but as from sincerity, but as from God, in the presence of God, we speak in Christ.
verses.after: For we are not like the many who peddle God's word. Instead, we speak in Christ with sincerity, as people sent from God and standing before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we are not like so many, peddling the word of God; but as from sincerity, but as from God, in the presence of God, we speak in Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps both rhetorical questions and the letter practice.
verses.before: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some do, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
verses.after: Are we beginning to recommend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some do, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some do, letters of recommendation to you or from you?

verses.rationale: Preserves the living-letter metaphor and public visibility.
verses.before: You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by all,
verses.after: You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by all,

verses.rationale: Keeps authorship, service, Spirit, and tablet contrasts.
verses.before: revealed as a letter of Christ, delivered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
verses.after: You show that you are Christ's letter, delivered through our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on tablets of human hearts.
verses.tsw_comparator: revealed as a letter of Christ, delivered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.

verses.rationale: Retains the direction and mediation of confidence.
verses.before: Such confidence we have through Christ toward God.
verses.after: We have this confidence toward God through Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Such confidence we have through Christ toward God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated sufficiency language and contrast.
verses.before: Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to claim anything as from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God,
verses.after: Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to consider anything as coming from ourselves; our sufficiency comes from God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to claim anything as from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God,

verses.rationale: Keeps covenantal service and the severe letter/Spirit contrast.
verses.before: who has made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant—not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
verses.after: He also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant—not of letter but of Spirit, for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
verses.tsw_comparator: who has made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant—not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

verses.rationale: Retains death, stone, glory, Israel, and the fading qualification.
verses.before: Now if the ministry of death, carved in letters on stone, came with glory, so that the people of Israel could not gaze at Moses’ face because of the glory of his face, a glory that was being set aside,
verses.after: Now if the ministry of death, engraved in letters on stones, came with glory, so that the Israelites could not look steadily at Moses' face because of its glory—a glory being brought to an end—
verses.tsw_comparator: Now if the ministry of death, carved in letters on stone, came with glory, so that the people of Israel could not gaze at Moses’ face because of the glory of his face, a glory that was being set aside,

verses.rationale: Preserves the lesser-to-greater question.
verses.before: how will not the ministry of the Spirit be with greater glory?
verses.after: how much more will the ministry of the Spirit be in glory?
verses.tsw_comparator: how will not the ministry of the Spirit be with greater glory?

verses.rationale: Keeps the two ministries and abundance.
verses.before: For if there was glory in the ministry of condemnation, the ministry of righteousness must abound in glory even more.
verses.after: For if there was glory in the ministry of condemnation, much more does the ministry of righteousness overflow with glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if there was glory in the ministry of condemnation, the ministry of righteousness must abound in glory even more.

verses.rationale: Preserves the comparative paradox.
verses.before: Indeed, in this case, what once had glory has come to have no glory, because of the glory that surpasses it.
verses.after: Indeed, what had been glorified has not been glorified in this respect because of the glory that surpasses it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, in this case, what once had glory has come to have no glory, because of the glory that surpasses it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the temporal and glory contrast.
verses.before: For if what was being set aside came through glory, much more what remains is in glory.
verses.after: For if what was being brought to an end came through glory, much more is what remains in glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if what was being set aside came through glory, much more what remains is in glory.

verses.rationale: Preserves hope as the ground of frankness.
verses.before: Since, then, we have such a hope, we act with great boldness,
verses.after: Therefore, since we have such a hope, we act with great boldness,
verses.tsw_comparator: Since, then, we have such a hope, we act with great boldness,

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses, veil, gaze, and end without harmonizing the image.
verses.before: not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face so that the people of Israel might not gaze at the end of what was being set aside.
verses.after: not like Moses, who put a veil over his face so the Israelites would not gaze at the end of what was being brought to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face so that the people of Israel might not gaze at the end of what was being set aside.

verses.rationale: Retains hardening, continuing veil, and Christological removal.
verses.before: But their minds were hardened. For to this day, when the old covenant is read, the same veil remains, not being lifted, because it is set aside in Christ.
verses.after: But their minds were hardened. For to this very day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant; it is not lifted, because only in Christ is it taken away.
verses.tsw_comparator: But their minds were hardened. For to this day, when the old covenant is read, the same veil remains, not being lifted, because it is set aside in Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps the present reading image and singular heart.
verses.before: Indeed, to this day whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their hearts;
verses.after: Indeed, to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, to this day whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their hearts;

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional turning and removal.
verses.before: but whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
verses.after: But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is removed.
verses.tsw_comparator: but whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

verses.rationale: Keeps the dense identification and freedom statement.
verses.before: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
verses.after: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

verses.rationale: Retains mirror ambiguity, progressive transformation, image, and source.
verses.before: And all of us, with unveiled face, seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as from the Lord, the Spirit.
verses.after: And all of us, with unveiled faces, beholding as in a mirror the Lord's glory, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as from the Lord, the Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: And all of us, with unveiled face, seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as from the Lord, the Spirit.

verses.rationale: Keeps ministry grounded in mercy and the resulting resolve.
verses.before: So, since we have this ministry by the mercy of God, we do not lose heart.
verses.after: Therefore, since we have this ministry because we received mercy, we do not lose heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, since we have this ministry by the mercy of God, we do not lose heart.

verses.rationale: Preserves renunciation, ethical contrasts, conscience, and Godward accountability.
verses.before: But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness nor falsifying the word of God, but by the open statement of the truth commending ourselves to every conscience in the sight of God.
verses.after: Instead, we have renounced secret, shameful things. We do not walk in deceit or distort God's word, but by openly presenting the truth we commend ourselves to every human conscience before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness nor falsifying the word of God, but by the open statement of the truth commending ourselves to every conscience in the sight of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the veil motif and audience.
verses.before: And even if our good news is veiled, it is veiled to people who are perishing,
verses.after: Even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing.
verses.tsw_comparator: And even if our good news is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing,

verses.rationale: Preserves agency, blindness, light, glory, and image.
verses.before: in whose case the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, so that they might not see the light of the good news of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
verses.after: In their case, the god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers so that the light of the gospel of Christ's glory, who is God's image, would not shine on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: in whose case the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, so that they might not see the light of the good news of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the object of proclamation and servant relation.
verses.before: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.
verses.after: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants because of Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.

verses.rationale: Retains creation echo, heart, knowledge, glory, and Christ's face.
verses.before: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
verses.after: For the God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” is the one who shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of God's glory in the face of Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps fragile-container image and divine source of power.
verses.before: But we have this treasure in clay jars, so that the surpassing power may be from God and not from us.
verses.after: But we have this treasure in clay jars so that the extraordinary power may be God's and not from us.
verses.tsw_comparator: But we have this treasure in clay jars, so that the surpassing power may be from God and not from us.

verses.rationale: Preserves both real harms and their limits.
verses.before: We are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not driven to despair;
verses.after: We are afflicted in every way but not crushed, perplexed but not driven to despair,
verses.tsw_comparator: We are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not driven to despair;

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired bodily and relational contrasts.
verses.before: persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed—
verses.after: persecuted but not abandoned, struck down but not destroyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed—

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily death/life correspondence.
verses.before: always carrying in the body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our bodies.
verses.after: We always carry around in the body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
verses.tsw_comparator: always carrying in the body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our bodies.

verses.rationale: Keeps passive exposure to death and mortal embodiment.
verses.before: For we who live are always being given over to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our mortal flesh.
verses.after: For we who live are continually being handed over to death because of Jesus, so that Jesus' life may also be revealed in our mortal flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we who live are always being given over to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our mortal flesh.

verses.rationale: Retains the stark apostolic/community contrast.
verses.before: So death is at work in us, but life in you.
verses.after: So death is at work in us, but life in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: So death is at work in us, but life in you.

verses.rationale: Keeps scriptural quotation and repeated faith/speech logic.
verses.before: But having the same spirit of faith according to what has been written, “I believed, therefore I spoke,” we also believe, and therefore we also speak,
verses.after: But since we have the same spirit of faith, according to what is written, “I believed; therefore I spoke,” we also believe, and therefore we speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: But having the same spirit of faith according to what has been written, “I believed, therefore I spoke,” we also believe, and therefore we also speak,

verses.rationale: Preserves resurrection agent and joint presentation.
verses.before: knowing that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with Jesus and will present us with you.
verses.after: We know that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us together with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: knowing that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with Jesus and will present us with you.

verses.rationale: Keeps communal spread, thanksgiving, and glory.
verses.before: For everything are for your sake, so that grace, increasing through the many, may cause thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.
verses.after: For all this is for your sake, so that grace, as it extends through more and more people, may cause thanksgiving to overflow to God's glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all things are for your sake, so that grace, increasing through the many, may cause thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.

verses.rationale: Retains bodily deterioration and inward renewal without denial.
verses.before: So we do not lose heart. Even though our outer person is wasting away, our inner person is being renewed day by day.
verses.after: Therefore we do not lose heart. Even though our outer person is wasting away, our inner person is being renewed day by day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore we do not lose heart. Even though our outer person is wasting away, our inner person is being renewed day by day.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's provocative light/weight and temporal contrast.
verses.before: For this light affliction is preparing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure,
verses.after: For our momentary light affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure,
verses.tsw_comparator: For this light affliction is preparing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure,

verses.rationale: Preserves gaze, seen/unseen, and temporal contrast.
verses.before: as we look not to the things that are seen but to the things that are unseen; for the things that are seen are temporary, but the things that are unseen are eternal.
verses.after: as we look not at what is seen but at what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.
verses.tsw_comparator: as we look not to the things that are seen but to the things that are unseen; for the things that are seen are temporary, but the things that are unseen are eternal.

verses.rationale: Keeps tent/building contrast and divine origin.
verses.before: For we know that if the earthly tent we live in is destroyed, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
verses.after: For we know that if our earthly tent-house is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in the heavens, not made by human hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we know that if the earthly tent we live in is destroyed, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

verses.rationale: Preserves groaning and the unusual clothing-over-dwelling image.
verses.before: For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our dwelling from heaven—
verses.after: For in this tent we groan, longing to put on our dwelling from heaven over it,
verses.tsw_comparator: For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our dwelling from heaven—

verses.rationale: Keeps the marked source uncertainty and nakedness contrast.
verses.before: if indeed, when we have been clothed, we will not be found naked.
verses.after: if indeed, once clothed, we will not be found naked.
verses.tsw_comparator: if indeed, when we have been clothed, we will not be found naked.

verses.rationale: Retains burden, clothing sequence, and swallowed-up image.
verses.before: For while we are in this tent, we groan, being burdened—not because we want to be unclothed, but further clothed, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
verses.after: For while we are in this tent, we groan under a burden, because we do not want to be unclothed but further clothed, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
verses.tsw_comparator: For while we are in this tent, we groan, being burdened—not because we want to be unclothed, but further clothed, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine preparation and commercial pledge image.
verses.before: The one who has prepared us for this very thing is God, who has given us the Spirit as a first pledge.
verses.after: The one who prepared us for this very thing is God, who gave us the Spirit as a down payment.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who has prepared us for this very thing is God, who has given us the Spirit as a first pledge.

verses.rationale: Preserves home/away wordplay and bodily location.
verses.before: So we are always confident, even though we know that while we are at home in the body we are away from the Lord—
verses.after: So we are always confident, knowing that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore we are always confident, even though we know that while we are at home in the body we are away from the Lord—

verses.rationale: Keeps the concise governing contrast.
verses.before: for we walk by trust, not by sight.
verses.after: for we walk by faith, not by sight.
verses.tsw_comparator: for we walk by faith, not by sight.

verses.rationale: Retains preference and reversed home/away pair.
verses.before: Yet we are confident, and we would rather be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
verses.after: Yes, we are confident, and we would rather be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet we are confident, and we would rather be away from the body and at home with the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps both conditions and the active aim.
verses.before: So whether we are at home or away, we make it our aim to be pleasing to him.
verses.after: Therefore, whether at home or away, we make it our ambition to please him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So whether we are at home or away, we make it our aim to be pleasing to him.

verses.rationale: Preserves universal appearance, bodily deeds, and moral alternatives.
verses.before: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each may receive what is due for what has been done in the body, whether good or bad.
verses.after: For all of us must appear before Christ's judgment seat, so that each may receive what is due for what was done through the body, whether good or worthless.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each may receive what is due for what has been done in the body, whether good or bad.

verses.rationale: Keeps persuasion, divine disclosure, and conscience.
verses.before: So, knowing the fear of the Lord, we persuade others; but what we are is known to God, and I hope that it is also known to your consciences.
verses.after: Therefore, knowing the fear of the Lord, we persuade people. But we are fully known to God, and I hope we are also fully known to your consciences.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, knowing the fear of the Lord, we persuade others; but what we are is known to God, and I hope that it is also known to your consciences.

verses.rationale: Preserves the denied self-commendation and appearance/heart contrast.
verses.before: We are not commending ourselves to you again but giving you an occasion to boast about us, so that you may have an answer for people who boast in outward appearance and not in the heart.
verses.after: We are not recommending ourselves to you again, but giving you an opportunity to boast about us, so that you may answer those who boast in outward appearance and not in the heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: We are not commending ourselves to you again but giving you an occasion to boast about us, so that you may have an answer for those who boast in outward appearance and not in the heart.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two possible judgments and beneficiaries.
verses.before: For if we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
verses.after: For if we are out of our minds, it is for God; if we are sound-minded, it is for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the force of love and compact representative logic.
verses.before: For the love of Christ compels us, because we have concluded this: one has died for all; therefore all have died.
verses.after: For Christ's love compels us, because we have concluded this: one died for all; therefore all died.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the love of Christ compels us, because we have concluded this: one has died for all; therefore all have died.

verses.rationale: Keeps death, resurrection, and transformed allegiance.
verses.before: And he died for all, so that people who live might no longer live for themselves but for the one who died and was raised for them.
verses.after: And he died for all so that those who live would no longer live for themselves, but for the one who died and was raised for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he died for all, so that those who live might no longer live for themselves but for the one who died and was raised for them.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated regard and chronological change.
verses.before: From now on, therefore, we regard no one according to the flesh; even though we once regarded Christ according to the flesh, we regard him thus no longer.
verses.after: So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Even if we once regarded Christ according to the flesh, we no longer regard him that way.
verses.tsw_comparator: From now on, therefore, we regard no one according to the flesh; even though we once regarded Christ according to the flesh, we regard him thus no longer.

verses.rationale: Keeps the verbless exclamation and creation contrast.
verses.before: So if someone is in Christ, there is a new creation: the old has passed away; look, the new has come.
verses.after: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ—new creation! The old things have passed away; look, new things have come.
verses.tsw_comparator: So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: the old has passed away; behold, the new has come.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine initiative and entrusted ministry.
verses.before: All this is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation,
verses.after: All this is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
verses.tsw_comparator: All this is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation,

verses.rationale: Keeps world scope, non-counting, and deposited message.
verses.before: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and entrusting to us the message of reconciliation.
verses.after: That is, in Christ God was reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and he entrusted the message of reconciliation to us.
verses.tsw_comparator: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and entrusting to us the message of reconciliation.

verses.rationale: Preserves representative office and direct appeal.
verses.before: So we are ambassadors for Christ, since God is making an appeal through us; we implore you on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God.
verses.after: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making his appeal through us. We plead on Christ's behalf: be reconciled to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, since God is making an appeal through us; we implore you on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the severe sin/righteousness exchange without explanatory expansion.
verses.before: The one who knew no sin, God made to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
verses.after: God made the one who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become God's righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who knew no sin, God made to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves joint work, appeal, and risk of empty reception.
verses.before: And working together with him, we also urge you not to receive the grace of God in vain.
verses.after: Working together with God, we also urge you not to receive God's grace in vain.
verses.tsw_comparator: And working together with him, we also urge you not to receive the grace of God in vain.

verses.rationale: Keeps quotation, repeated time, and urgent double look.
verses.before: For he says, “In an acceptable time I heard you, and in a day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation.
verses.after: For he says, “At an acceptable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I helped you.” Look, now is the acceptable time; look, now is the day of salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he says, “In an acceptable time I heard you, and in a day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation.

verses.rationale: Preserves conduct and reputational purpose.
verses.before: We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no fault may be found with the ministry,
verses.after: We put no obstacle in anyone's way, so that the ministry will not be discredited.
verses.tsw_comparator: We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no fault may be found with the ministry,

verses.rationale: Keeps the servant claim and opening catalogue.
verses.before: but in everything commending ourselves as servants of God: in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
verses.after: Instead, in everything we commend ourselves as God's servants: through great endurance, in afflictions, hardships, and distress,
verses.tsw_comparator: but in everything commending ourselves as servants of God: in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,

verses.rationale: Names the real harms and bodily costs.
verses.before: in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in sleepless nights, in hunger;
verses.after: in beatings, imprisonments, and riots, in hard work, sleepless nights, and hunger,
verses.tsw_comparator: in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in sleepless nights, in hunger;

verses.rationale: Retains the ethical and spiritual means.
verses.before: in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in genuine love,
verses.after: in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness, in the Holy Spirit and sincere love,
verses.tsw_comparator: in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in genuine love,

verses.rationale: Keeps truth, power, and two-handed military image.
verses.before: in truthful speech, and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and for the left,
verses.after: in truthful speech and God's power, with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and the left,
verses.tsw_comparator: in truthful speech, and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and for the left,

verses.rationale: Preserves public reversals and perception/reality.
verses.before: through honor and dishonor, through slander and praise; regarded as deceivers and yet true,
verses.after: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; treated as deceivers, yet truthful;
verses.tsw_comparator: through honor and dishonor, through slander and praise; regarded as deceivers and yet true,

verses.rationale: Keeps the escalating paradoxes and punishment.
verses.before: as unknown and yet known; as dying, and look, we live; as disciplined, and not killed;
verses.after: as unknown, yet fully known; as dying, yet look—we live; as punished, yet not put to death;
verses.tsw_comparator: as unknown and yet known; as dying, and behold, we live; as disciplined, and not killed;

verses.rationale: Retains sorrow, poverty, and possession paradoxes.
verses.before: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything.
verses.after: as grieving, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct address and widened-heart image.
verses.before: We have spoken openly to you, Corinthians; our heart has been opened wide.
verses.after: We have spoken openly to you, Corinthians; our heart has opened wide.
verses.tsw_comparator: We have spoken openly to you, Corinthians; our heart has been opened wide.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated constriction and inward location.
verses.before: You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted in your own affections.
verses.after: You are not confined by us, but you are confined in your own affections.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted in your own affections.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal appeal and parental address.
verses.before: In return—I speak as to children—open wide your hearts also.
verses.after: In return—I speak as to my children—open wide to us also.
verses.tsw_comparator: In return—I speak as to children—open wide your hearts also.

verses.rationale: Retains yoking image and paired rhetorical contrasts.
verses.before: Do not be mismatched with unbelievers. For what partnership has righteousness with lawlessness? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?
verses.after: Do not be mismatched with unbelievers. For what partnership do righteousness and lawlessness have? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be mismatched with unbelievers. For what partnership has righteousness with lawlessness? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?

verses.rationale: Keeps the proper name and two relational questions.
verses.before: What accord has Christ with Belial? Or what portion does a believer share with an unbeliever?
verses.after: What agreement does Christ have with Beliar? Or what share does a believer have with an unbeliever?
verses.tsw_comparator: What accord has Christ with Belial? Or what portion does a believer share with an unbeliever?

verses.rationale: Preserves communal temple identity and covenant quotation.
verses.before: What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, “I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
verses.after: What agreement does God's temple have with idols? For we are the living God's temple, as God said: “I will dwell and walk among them; I will be their God, and they will be my people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, “I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

verses.rationale: Keeps the quoted commands and divine reception.
verses.before: So go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean; then I will welcome you,
verses.after: “Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Do not touch what is unclean, and I will welcome you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore go out from their midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean; then I will welcome you,

verses.rationale: Retains both gendered kinship terms and divine title.
verses.before: and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty.”
verses.after: “I will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty.”

verses.rationale: Keeps promise-grounded communal exhortation and whole-person scope.
verses.before: So, since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God.
verses.after: Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, since we have these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of body and spirit, bringing holiness to completion in the fear of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the opening metaphor and three denials.
verses.before: Make room for us; we have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have taken advantage of no one.
verses.after: Make room for us. We wronged no one, ruined no one, exploited no one.
verses.tsw_comparator: Make room for us; we have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have taken advantage of no one.

verses.rationale: Keeps denied condemnation and intense solidarity.
verses.before: I do not say this to condemn you, for I have said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
verses.after: I do not say this to condemn you, for I have said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and live together.
verses.tsw_comparator: I do not say this to condemn you, for I have said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated abundance amid suffering.
verses.before: I have great boldness toward you; I have great boasting on your behalf; I am filled with comfort; in all our affliction I overflow with joy.
verses.after: I have great confidence in you and great pride in you. I am filled with comfort; I overflow with joy in all our affliction.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have great boldness toward you; I have great boasting on your behalf; I am filled with comfort; in all our affliction I overflow with joy.

verses.rationale: Keeps geography, bodily unrest, and external/internal harms.
verses.before: For even when we came into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were afflicted in every way—conflicts without, fears within.
verses.after: For even when we came to Macedonia, our bodies had no rest; we were afflicted in every way—conflicts outside, fears within.
verses.tsw_comparator: For even when we came into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were afflicted in every way—conflicts without, fears within.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine characterization and human means.
verses.before: Yet God, who comforts the lowly, comforted us by the coming of Titus,
verses.after: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by Titus's arrival,
verses.tsw_comparator: But God, who comforts the lowly, comforted us by the coming of Titus,

verses.rationale: Keeps layered comfort and the three reports.
verses.before: and not only by his coming but also by the comfort with which he was comforted by you, as he reported to us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced still more.
verses.after: and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he received from you. He told us of your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced even more.
verses.tsw_comparator: and not only by his coming but also by the comfort with which he was comforted by you, as he reported to us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced still more.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's emotional reversal and temporal limit.
verses.before: For even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it—though I did regret it—for I see that the letter caused you sorrow, though only for a time.
verses.after: Even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Though I did regret it—for I see that the letter caused you sorrow, even if only for a while—
verses.tsw_comparator: For even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it—though I did regret it—for I see that the letter caused you sorrow, though only for a time.

verses.rationale: Keeps distinction between harm and restorative result.
verses.before: Now I rejoice, not because you were grieved, but because you were grieved into repentance; for you experienced a grief according to God, so that you suffered no loss through us.
verses.after: now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led to repentance. For you felt sorrow in accordance with God, so that you suffered no loss through us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I rejoice, not because you were grieved, but because you were grieved into repentance; for you experienced a grief according to God, so that you suffered no loss through us.

verses.rationale: Retains the two kinds of sorrow and outcomes.
verses.before: For grief according to God produces a repentance leading to salvation without regret, but the grief of the world produces death.
verses.after: For godly sorrow produces repentance leading to salvation, which brings no regret; but worldly sorrow produces death.
verses.tsw_comparator: For grief according to God produces a repentance leading to salvation without regret, but the grief of the world produces death.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic list and justice language.
verses.before: For see what earnestness this very grief according to God has produced in you—what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what readiness to see justice done. In every way you have proved yourselves to be pure in this matter.
verses.after: Just look at what this very godly sorrow produced in you: what earnestness, what defense, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what readiness to see justice done! In every way you showed yourselves innocent in the matter.
verses.tsw_comparator: For see what earnestness this very grief according to God has produced in you—what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what readiness to see justice done. In every way you have proved yourselves to be pure in this matter.

verses.rationale: Keeps both harmed parties and stated revelatory purpose.
verses.before: So although I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did the wrong, nor for the sake of the one who suffered the wrong, but so that your earnestness for us might be revealed to you in the sight of God.
verses.after: So although I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did wrong, nor for the sake of the one wronged, but so that your earnest concern for us might be revealed to you before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: So although I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did the wrong, nor for the sake of the one who suffered the wrong, but so that your earnestness for us might be revealed to you in the sight of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves layered comfort and communal refreshment.
verses.before: So we are comforted. And in addition to our comfort, we rejoiced still more at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
verses.after: Because of this we have been comforted. And beyond our own comfort, we rejoiced even more at Titus's joy, because all of you refreshed his spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore we are comforted. And in addition to our comfort, we rejoiced still more at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.

verses.rationale: Keeps shame/true contrast and audience distinction.
verses.before: For whatever I boasted to him about you, I was not put to shame; but just as everything we said to you was true, so also our boasting before Titus has proved true.
verses.after: For if I boasted to him about you in any way, I was not put to shame. Just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting before Titus also proved true.
verses.tsw_comparator: For whatever I boasted to him about you, I was not put to shame; but just as everything we said to you was true, so also our boasting before Titus has proved true.

verses.rationale: Preserves memory, affection, communal obedience, and response.
verses.before: And his affection for you is even greater, as he remembers the obedience of all of you, how you received him with fear and trembling.
verses.after: His affection for you grows even greater as he remembers the obedience of all of you and how you received him with fear and trembling.
verses.tsw_comparator: And his affection for you is even greater, as he remembers the obedience of all of you, how you received him with fear and trembling.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unqualified closing confidence.
verses.before: I rejoice, because in everything I have confidence in you.
verses.after: I rejoice because I have complete confidence in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I rejoice, because in everything I have confidence in you.

verses.rationale: Preserves disclosure, divine gift, and regional churches.
verses.before: We reveal to you, brothers and sisters, the grace of God that has been given among the churches of Macedonia,
verses.after: Now, brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace of God given among the churches of Macedonia.
verses.tsw_comparator: We make known to you, brothers and sisters, the grace of God that has been given among the churches of Macedonia,

verses.rationale: Keeps affliction and poverty real while preserving the abundance wordplay.
verses.before: that in a severe testing of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their extreme poverty overflowed in the wealth of their generosity.
verses.after: In a severe test of affliction, their overflowing joy and their deep poverty overflowed into a wealth of generosity.
verses.tsw_comparator: that in a severe testing of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their extreme poverty overflowed in the wealth of their generosity.

verses.rationale: Retains measure, excess, and voluntary agency.
verses.before: For according to their means, I can testify, and beyond their means, they gave of their own accord,
verses.after: For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond their ability, entirely of their own accord,
verses.tsw_comparator: For according to their means, I can testify, and beyond their means, they gave of their own accord,

verses.rationale: Keeps their initiative and service as participation.
verses.before: begging us earnestly for the favor of participating in the ministry to the holy ones,
verses.after: pleading with us insistently for the grace and fellowship of serving the saints.
verses.tsw_comparator: begging us earnestly for the favor of participating in the ministry to the holy ones,

verses.rationale: Preserves sequence and divine grounding.
verses.before: and this not as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us by the will of God.
verses.after: And not merely as we expected: they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us through God's will.
verses.tsw_comparator: and this not as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us by the will of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps Titus's prior action and completing task.
verses.before: So we urged Titus that as he had begun, so he should also complete among you this gracious work.
verses.after: So we urged Titus that, just as he had begun earlier, he should also bring this gracious work among you to completion.
verses.tsw_comparator: So we urged Titus that as he had begun, so he should also complete among you this gracious work.

verses.rationale: Retains the variant-marked love phrase and repeated overflow.
verses.before: But as you abound in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all earnestness, and in the love we have awakened in you—see that you abound in this gracious work also.
verses.after: But just as you overflow in everything—in faith, speech, knowledge, every kind of earnestness, and the love from us that is among you—see that you also overflow in this grace.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as you abound in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all earnestness, and in the love we have awakened in you—see that you abound in this gracious work also.

verses.rationale: Preserves non-command and comparative test.
verses.before: I say this not as a command, but to test the genuineness of your love by the earnestness of others.
verses.after: I am not saying this as a command, but I am testing the genuineness of your love through the earnestness of others.
verses.tsw_comparator: I say this not as a command, but to test the genuineness of your love by the earnestness of others.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rich/poor reversal as Christ's grace.
verses.before: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you by his poverty might become rich.
verses.after: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ: though he was rich, for your sake he became poor, so that through his poverty you might become rich.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you by his poverty might become rich.

verses.rationale: Preserves advice, benefit, time, action, and will.
verses.before: And in this matter I give my judgment: this benefits you, who a year ago began not only to do this but also to desire it.
verses.after: And in this matter I give my judgment, for this benefits you: last year you were the first not only to do this, but also to desire it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And in this matter I give my judgment: this benefits you, who a year ago began not only to do this but also to desire it.

verses.rationale: Keeps eagerness/completion correspondence and available means.
verses.before: So now complete the doing of it, so that your readiness in desiring it may be matched by completion according to what you have.
verses.after: Now also complete the doing, so that your completion from what you have may match your eager desire.
verses.tsw_comparator: So now complete the doing of it, so that your readiness in desiring it may be matched by completion according to what you have.

verses.rationale: Preserves acceptance without impossible demand.
verses.before: For if the readiness is present, it is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
verses.after: For if the eagerness is present, the gift is acceptable according to what a person has, not according to what the person does not have.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if the readiness is present, it is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit rejection of burden shifting and aim.
verses.before: For I do not mean that others should be relieved and you burdened,
verses.after: I do not mean that others should have relief while you have affliction, but that there should be equality.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I do not mean that others should be relieved and you burdened,

verses.rationale: Preserves present reciprocity and repeated equality.
verses.before: but that there may be equality. At the present time your abundance meets their need, so that their abundance may also meet your need, that there may be equality.
verses.after: At the present time, your abundance should meet their need, so that their abundance may also meet your need, and in this way there may be equality.
verses.tsw_comparator: but that there may be equality. At the present time your abundance meets their need, so that their abundance may also meet your need, that there may be equality.

verses.rationale: Keeps the scriptural balance without added referent.
verses.before: As it is written, “The one who gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who gathered little had no lack.”
verses.after: As it is written, “The one who gathered much had no excess, and the one who gathered little had no lack.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As it is written, “The one who gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who gathered little had no lack.”

verses.rationale: Preserves gratitude, divine action, and Titus's inward concern.
verses.before: But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same earnest care I have for you.
verses.after: But thanks be to God, who put the same earnest concern for you into Titus's heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same earnest care I have for you.

verses.rationale: Keeps response and voluntary action.
verses.before: For he not only accepted our appeal, but being himself very earnest, he went to you of his own accord.
verses.after: For he welcomed our appeal and, being even more earnest, went to you of his own accord.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he not only accepted our appeal, but being himself very earnest, he went to you of his own accord.

verses.rationale: Retains anonymity, kinship, praise, and sphere.
verses.before: With him we are sending the brother who is praised among all the churches for his work in the good news,
verses.after: We sent with him the brother praised throughout all the churches for his work in the gospel.
verses.tsw_comparator: With him we are sending the brother who is praised among all the churches for his work in the good news,

verses.rationale: Preserves church appointment and accountable administration.
verses.before: and not only that, but he has been appointed by the churches to travel with us in this gracious work, which is being administered by us for the glory of the Lord himself and to show our readiness.
verses.after: Not only that, but he was also appointed by the churches to travel with us as we administer this gracious gift for the Lord's own glory and to show our eagerness.
verses.tsw_comparator: and not only that, but he has been appointed by the churches to travel with us in this gracious work, which is being administered by us for the glory of the Lord himself and to show our readiness.

verses.rationale: Keeps preventive accountability for a large sum.
verses.before: We take this course so that no one should blame us about this generous gift that is being administered by us,
verses.after: We are taking this precaution so that no one can criticize us concerning this generous gift we are administering.
verses.tsw_comparator: We take this course so that no one should blame us about this generous gift that is being administered by us,

verses.rationale: Preserves dual audience for integrity.
verses.before: for we aim at what is honorable not only in the sight of the Lord but also in the sight of others.
verses.after: For we take care to do what is honorable not only before the Lord, but also before people.
verses.tsw_comparator: for we aim at what is honorable not only in the sight of the Lord but also in the sight of others.

verses.rationale: Keeps anonymity, testing, and increased eagerness.
verses.before: And with them we are sending our brother whom we have often tested and found earnest in many matters, but who is now even more earnest because of his great confidence in you.
verses.after: We sent with them our brother whom we have often tested and found earnest in many matters, and now he is much more earnest because of his great confidence in you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And with them we are sending our brother whom we have often tested and found earnest in many matters, but who is now even more earnest because of his great confidence in you.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct roles and the plural church-apostle sense.
verses.before: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for your sake; and as for our brothers and sisters, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ.
verses.after: As for Titus, he is my partner and coworker for you. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for your sake; and as for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps public demonstration and reciprocal reputation.
verses.before: So show them the proof of your love and of our boasting about you before the churches.
verses.after: Therefore show them, before the churches, the proof of your love and of our boasting about you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore show them the proof of your love and of our boasting about you before the churches.

verses.rationale: Preserves the transition and ironic confidence.
verses.before: For concerning the ministry to the holy ones, it is unnecessary for me to write to you,
verses.after: Now concerning the service for the saints, it is unnecessary for me to write to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For concerning the ministry to the holy ones, it is unnecessary for me to write to you,

verses.rationale: Keeps regions, time, boasting, and motivating effect.
verses.before: for I know your readiness, of which I boast about you to the Macedonians, that Achaia has been ready since last year; and your zeal has stirred up most of them.
verses.after: For I know your eagerness, which I boast about to the Macedonians: “Achaia has been ready since last year.” And your zeal has stirred up most of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: for I know your readiness, of which I boast about you to the Macedonians, that Achaia has been ready since last year; and your zeal has stirred up most of them.

verses.rationale: Preserves precaution and stated expectation.
verses.before: Yet I am sending the brothers and sisters so that our boasting about you may not prove empty in this matter, so that you may be ready, as I said you would be,
verses.after: But I sent the brothers so that our boasting about you in this matter would not prove empty, but that you would be ready, just as I said.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I am sending the brothers so that our boasting about you may not prove empty in this matter, so that you may be ready, as I said you would be,

verses.rationale: Keeps hypothetical exposure and Paul's qualification.
verses.before: lest if some Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—not to say you—would be put to shame in this confidence.
verses.after: Otherwise, if Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed in this confidence.
verses.tsw_comparator: lest if some Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—not to say you—would be put to shame in this confidence.

verses.rationale: Preserves advance preparation and generosity/coercion contrast.
verses.before: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers and sisters to go on ahead to you and arrange in advance the generous gift you had promised, so that it may be ready as a blessing and not as something forced.
verses.after: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to go to you in advance and prepare beforehand the generous gift you had already promised, so that it would be ready as a gift and not as something extorted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to go on ahead to you and arrange in advance the generous gift you had promised, so that it may be ready as a blessing and not as something forced.

verses.rationale: Keeps agrarian image and repeated measure.
verses.before: The point is this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows generously will also reap generously.
verses.after: The point is this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows with blessings will also reap with blessings.
verses.tsw_comparator: The point is this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows generously will also reap generously.

verses.rationale: Preserves inward decision, freedom, and quoted reason.
verses.before: Each one must give as he has decided in his heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
verses.after: Each person should give as decided in the heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each one must give as he has decided in his heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.

verses.rationale: Keeps deliberate repetitions of every/all.
verses.before: God can make all grace abound to you, so that having all sufficiency in everything at all times, you may abound in every good work.
verses.after: And God is able to make every grace overflow to you, so that in everything, always having everything you need, you may overflow in every good work.
