verses.tsw_comparator: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that having all sufficiency in everything at all times, you may abound in every good work.

verses.rationale: Retains the quotation's actions and enduring righteousness.
verses.before: As it is written, “He has distributed freely; he has given to the poor; his righteousness endures forever.”
verses.after: As it is written, “He scattered; he gave to the poor. His righteousness remains forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As it is written, “He has distributed freely; he has given to the poor; his righteousness endures forever.”

verses.rationale: Keeps provider, agricultural chain, and moral harvest.
verses.before: The one who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
verses.after: The one who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.

verses.rationale: Preserves enrichment's purpose and mediating service.
verses.before: You will be enriched in every way for all generosity, which through us produces thanksgiving to God.
verses.after: You will be enriched in every way for every kind of generosity, which through us produces thanksgiving to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will be enriched in every way for all generosity, which through us produces thanksgiving to God.

verses.rationale: Keeps material need and worshipful result together.
verses.before: For the ministry of this service is not only supplying the needs of the holy ones but is also overflowing in many thanksgivings to God.
verses.after: For the ministry of this service not only supplies what the saints lack, but also overflows in many thanksgivings to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the ministry of this service is not only supplying the needs of the holy ones but is also overflowing in many thanksgivings to God.

verses.rationale: Preserves tested service, confession, and broad sharing.
verses.before: Through the proof of this ministry, they glorify God because of your obedience in the confession of the good news of Christ and the generosity of your sharing with them and with all.
verses.after: Because this ministry has proved your character, they will glorify God for the obedience of your confession of Christ's gospel and for the generosity of your sharing with them and with everyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Through the proof of this ministry, they glorify God because of your obedience in the confession of the good news of Christ and the generosity of your sharing with them and with all.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal prayer, affection, and grace.
verses.before: And in their prayer for you, they long for you because of the surpassing grace of God upon you.
verses.after: And in their prayer for you they will long for you because of God's surpassing grace upon you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And in their prayer for you, they long for you because of the surpassing grace of God upon you.

verses.rationale: Retains the brief doxological exclamation.
verses.before: Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift.
verses.after: Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift!
verses.tsw_comparator: Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's self-reference and quotes the opponents' characterization.
verses.before: Now I, Paul, myself appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ—I who am humble when face to face with you, but bold toward you when absent—
verses.after: Now I, Paul, personally appeal to you by Christ's gentleness and graciousness—I who am “humble” when face-to-face with you, but “bold” toward you when absent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I, Paul, myself appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ—I who am humble when face to face with you, but bold toward you when absent—

verses.rationale: Preserves requested avoidance, anticipated action, and accusation.
verses.before: I beg that when I am present I may not have to be bold with the confidence by which I consider showing boldness against some who think of us as walking according to the flesh.
verses.after: I ask that, when present, I will not have to be bold with the confidence I expect to show against some who think we walk according to the flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: I beg that when I am present I may not have to be bold with the confidence by which I consider showing boldness against some who think of us as walking according to the flesh.

verses.rationale: Keeps embodied life distinct from fleshly warfare.
verses.before: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh,
verses.after: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh,

verses.rationale: Preserves military metaphor and enjambment into the next verse.
verses.before: for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh but have divine power for the tearing down of strongholds.
verses.after: For the weapons of our warfare are not fleshly but powerful through God for tearing down strongholds. We tear down arguments
verses.tsw_comparator: for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh but have divine power for the tearing down of strongholds.

verses.rationale: Keeps elevated resistance, captivity, and directed obedience.
verses.before: We tear down arguments and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive to the obedience of Christ,
verses.after: and every proud obstacle raised against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive to obey Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: We tear down arguments and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and we take every thought captive to the obedience of Christ,

verses.rationale: Preserves readiness, punishment, and timing condition.
verses.before: being ready to punish every disobedience, when your obedience is complete.
verses.after: And we are ready to punish every disobedience once your obedience is complete.
verses.tsw_comparator: being ready to punish every disobedience, when your obedience is complete.

verses.rationale: Keeps possible command, self-examination, and equal claim.
verses.before: Look at what is before your eyes. If someone is confident that he belongs to Christ, let him consider again that just as he belongs to Christ, so also do we.
verses.after: Look at what is right in front of you. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should consider this again about himself: just as he belongs to Christ, so do we.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look at what is before your eyes. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, let him consider again that just as he belongs to Christ, so also do we.

verses.rationale: Preserves authority's source and constructive limit.
verses.before: For even if I boast somewhat excessively about our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down, I will not be put to shame.
verses.after: For even if I boast somewhat more about our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.
verses.tsw_comparator: For even if I boast somewhat excessively about our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down, I will not be put to shame.

verses.rationale: Keeps the perceived intimidation explicit.
verses.before: I do not want to seem as if I am frightening you by my letters.
verses.after: I do not want to seem as though I am trying to frighten you through my letters.
verses.tsw_comparator: I do not want to seem as though I am frightening you by my letters.

verses.rationale: Retains the opponent's disparaging words and bodily reference.
verses.before: For they say, “His letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech of no account.”
verses.after: For someone says, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his bodily presence is weak and his speech amounts to nothing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For they say, “His letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech of no account.”

verses.rationale: Preserves word/deed and absence/presence parallel.
verses.before: Let such a person understand that what we say by letter when absent, we also do when present.
verses.after: Such a person should consider this: what we are in words through letters when absent, we will also be in action when present.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let such a person understand that what we say by letter when absent, we also do when present.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's irony and repeated self-comparison.
verses.before: For we do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves; but when they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they are without understanding.
verses.after: For we do not dare to place or compare ourselves with some who recommend themselves. But when they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they lack understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves; but when they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they are without understanding.

verses.rationale: Preserves measured field and divine assignment.
verses.before: But we will not boast beyond measure, but within the measure of the sphere that God has assigned to us—a measure that reaches even to you.
verses.after: We, however, will not boast beyond measure, but only according to the boundary God assigned to us—a boundary that extends even as far as you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But we will not boast beyond measure, but within the measure of the sphere that God has assigned to us—a measure that reaches even to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps geographic metaphor and actual arrival.
verses.before: For we are not overextending ourselves, as if we did not reach you, for we were the first to come even to you with the good news of Christ.
verses.after: For we are not overextending ourselves, as if we had not reached you, because we did reach as far as you with Christ's gospel.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we are not overextending ourselves, as though we did not reach you, for we were the first to come even to you with the good news of Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves denial, growth, and bounded expansion.
verses.before: We do not boast beyond measure in the labors of others, but our hope is that as your trust increases, our sphere among you may be enlarged still more,
verses.after: We do not boast beyond measure in the labors of others. But we hope that as your faith grows, our work among you will be greatly enlarged within our boundary,
verses.tsw_comparator: We do not boast beyond measure in the labors of others, but our hope is that as your faith increases, our sphere among you may be enlarged still more,

verses.rationale: Keeps future mission and refusal to claim another's labor.
verses.before: so that we may proclaim the good news in lands beyond you, without boasting in work already done in another’s sphere.
verses.after: so that we may proclaim the gospel in the regions beyond you, without boasting about work already prepared in someone else's field.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that we may proclaim the good news in lands beyond you, without boasting in work already done in another’s sphere.

verses.rationale: Retains the concise scriptural command.
verses.before: “Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.”
verses.after: “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.”

verses.rationale: Keeps self-commendation and divine approval contrast.
verses.before: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
verses.after: For it is not the one who recommends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord recommends.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ironic request and emphatic repetition.
verses.before: I wish you would bear with me in a little foolishness. Indeed, do bear with me.
verses.after: I wish you would put up with a little foolishness from me. Indeed, do put up with me!
verses.tsw_comparator: I wish you would bear with me in a little foolishness. Indeed, do bear with me.

verses.rationale: Keeps betrothal metaphor, gender, and divine jealousy.
verses.before: For I feel a divine jealousy for you, since I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
verses.after: For I am jealous for you with God's jealousy, because I promised you to one husband, to present you to Christ as a pure virgin.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I feel a divine jealousy for you, since I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves Eve, deception, mental corruption, and variant-marked purity.
verses.before: Yet I am afraid that just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your thoughts may be led astray from sincere and pure devotion to Christ.
verses.after: But I fear that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your minds may be corrupted from sincere and pure devotion to Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I am afraid that just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your thoughts may be led astray from sincere and pure devotion to Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps the threefold alternative and biting irony.
verses.before: For if someone comes and proclaims another Jesus than the one we proclaimed, or you receive a different spirit than the one you received, or a different good news than the one you accepted—you put up with it readily enough.
verses.after: For if someone comes proclaiming another Jesus whom we did not proclaim, or you receive a different spirit you did not receive, or a different gospel you did not accept, you put up with it well enough!
verses.tsw_comparator: For if someone comes and proclaims another Jesus than the one we proclaimed, or you receive a different spirit than the one you received, or a different good news than the one you accepted—you put up with it readily enough.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ironic designation and comparison.
verses.before: For I consider that I am not in the least inferior to these “super-apostles.”
verses.after: For I consider myself in no way inferior to those “super-apostles.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I consider that I am not in the least inferior to these “super-apostles.”

verses.rationale: Keeps speech/knowledge contrast and disclosure.
verses.before: Even if I am unskilled in speech, I am not so in knowledge; indeed, in every way we have made this plain to you in everything.
verses.after: Even if I am untrained in speech, I am not untrained in knowledge. In every way we have made this clear to you in all things.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even if I am unskilled in speech, I am not so in knowledge; indeed, in every way we have made this plain to you in all things.

verses.rationale: Preserves ironic question, reversal, and free proclamation.
verses.before: Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I proclaimed the good news of God to you free of charge?
verses.after: Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I proclaimed God's gospel to you without charge?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I proclaimed the good news of God to you free of charge?

verses.rationale: Retains Paul's deliberately harsh robbery metaphor.
verses.before: I robbed other churches, taking wages from them in order to serve you.
verses.after: I robbed other churches by accepting support in order to serve you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I robbed other churches, taking wages from them in order to serve you.

verses.rationale: Keeps material need, source of aid, and resolve.
verses.before: And when I was with you and was in need, I did not burden anyone; for the brothers and sisters who came from Macedonia supplied my need. So I kept myself from being a burden to you in any way, and will continue to do so.
verses.after: And when I was with you and in need, I did not burden anyone, for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied what I lacked. In everything I kept myself from being a burden to you, and I will continue to do so.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when I was with you and was in need, I did not burden anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my need. So I kept myself from being a burden to you in any way, and will continue to do so.

verses.rationale: Preserves solemn assertion and geography.
verses.before: As the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
verses.after: As surely as Christ's truth is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.

verses.rationale: Keeps the terse questions and divine witness.
verses.before: And why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do.
verses.after: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do.
verses.tsw_comparator: And why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated opportunity and polemical aim.
verses.before: And what I am doing I will continue to do, so that I may cut off the opportunity from people who desire an opportunity to be regarded just as we are in what they boast about.
verses.after: But what I do, I will continue to do, in order to cut off the opportunity from those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in what they boast about.
verses.tsw_comparator: And what I am doing I will continue to do, so that I may cut off the opportunity from those who desire an opportunity to be regarded just as we are in what they boast about.

verses.rationale: Keeps the direct accusations and disguise.
verses.before: For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.
verses.after: For such people are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.

verses.rationale: Retains Satan and deceptive transformation.
verses.before: And no wonder, for even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light.
verses.after: And no wonder, for Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
verses.tsw_comparator: And no wonder, for even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light.

verses.rationale: Keeps agent relation, disguise, and final outcome.
verses.before: So it is no great thing if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their deeds.
verses.after: So it is no great surprise if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their works.
verses.tsw_comparator: So it is no great thing if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their deeds.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated framing and conditional request.
verses.before: I repeat, let no one think me foolish; but if you do, then accept me as foolish, so that I too may boast a little.
verses.after: I say again: no one should think I am a fool. But if you do, then receive me even as a fool so that I too may boast a little.
verses.tsw_comparator: I repeat, let no one think me foolish; but if you do, then accept me as foolish, so that I too may boast a little.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's explicit qualification of his speech.
verses.before: What I am saying in this boastful confidence, I say not according to the Lord, but as in foolishness.
verses.after: What I am saying, I am not saying according to the Lord, but as in foolishness, with this confidence in boasting.
verses.tsw_comparator: What I am saying in this boastful confidence, I say not according to the Lord, but as in foolishness.

verses.rationale: Preserves stated reason and imitation.
verses.before: Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
verses.after: Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
verses.tsw_comparator: Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.

verses.rationale: Keeps sharp irony and direct address.
verses.before: For you gladly bear with fools, being wise yourselves.
verses.after: For you gladly put up with fools, since you yourselves are so wise!
verses.tsw_comparator: For you gladly bear with fools, being wise yourselves.

verses.rationale: Names domination, exploitation, arrogance, and physical violence.
verses.before: For you bear it if someone enslaves you, devours you, takes advantage of you, exalts himself, or strikes you in the face.
verses.after: Indeed, you put up with it if someone enslaves you, devours you, takes from you, exalts himself, or strikes you in the face.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you bear it if someone enslaves you, devours you, takes advantage of you, exalts himself, or strikes you in the face.

verses.rationale: Keeps sarcasm, weakness, and qualified rivalry.
verses.before: To my shame, I must say, we were too weak for that! But whatever anyone else dares to boast of—I am speaking in foolishness—I also dare.
verses.after: To our shame, I admit that we were too weak for that! But whatever anyone dares to boast about—I speak in foolishness—I also dare. But whatever anyone else dares to boast of—I am speaking in foolishness—I also dare.
verses.tsw_comparator: To my shame, I must say, we were too weak for that! But whatever anyone else dares to boast of—I am speaking in foolishness—I also dare.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three identities and clipped replies.
verses.before: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they offspring of Abraham? So am I.
verses.after: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they Abraham's offspring? So am I.
verses.tsw_comparator: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they offspring of Abraham? So am I.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's disclaimer and actual harms.
verses.before: Are they servants of Christ? I am speaking as one beside himself—I more so: in labors more abundant, in imprisonments more frequent, in beatings beyond measure, in deaths often.
verses.after: Are they servants of Christ? I am speaking like a madman: I am far more—in far more labors, far more imprisonments, countless beatings, and often near death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Are they servants of Christ? I am speaking as one beside himself—I more so: in labors more abundant, in imprisonments more frequent, in beatings beyond measure, in deaths often.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact number, agents, and punishment.
verses.before: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
verses.after: Five times I received from the Jews forty lashes minus one.
verses.tsw_comparator: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.

verses.rationale: Keeps all counts and bodily dangers.
verses.before: Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was shipwrecked; a night and a day I was adrift at sea;
verses.after: Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked; I spent a night and a day in the open sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was shipwrecked; a night and a day I was adrift at sea;

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated danger and all locations/groups.
verses.before: in journeys often, in dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from my own people, dangers from Gentiles, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brothers and sisters;
verses.after: I have often been on journeys, in danger from rivers, danger from robbers, danger from my own people, danger from Gentiles, danger in the city, danger in the wilderness, danger at sea, danger among false brothers,
verses.tsw_comparator: in journeys often, in dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from my own people, dangers from Gentiles, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brothers;

verses.rationale: Names deprivation without spiritualizing it.
verses.before: in toil and hardship, in sleepless nights often, in hunger and thirst, often without food, in cold and exposure.
verses.after: in toil and hardship, through many sleepless nights, in hunger and thirst, often without food, in cold and without enough clothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: in toil and hardship, in sleepless nights often, in hunger and thirst, often without food, in cold and exposure.

verses.rationale: Keeps the internal pressure and daily scope.
verses.before: And apart from other things, there is the daily pressure on me of my concern for all the churches.
verses.after: Besides everything else, there is the daily pressure on me: my concern for all the churches.
verses.tsw_comparator: And apart from other things, there is the daily pressure on me of my concern for all the churches.

verses.rationale: Preserves solidarity and fiery emotional image.
verses.before: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is caused to stumble, and I am not inflamed?
verses.after: Who is weak without my sharing their weakness? Who is made to stumble without my burning with distress?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is caused to stumble, and I am not inflamed?

verses.rationale: Keeps weakness as the chosen ground.
verses.before: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
verses.after: If I must boast, I will boast about the things that show my weakness.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.

verses.rationale: Preserves full title, blessing, and oath.
verses.before: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
verses.after: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus—the one blessed forever—knows that I am not lying.
verses.tsw_comparator: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.

verses.rationale: Keeps offices, ruler, place, and intended capture.
verses.before: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me,
verses.after: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas guarded the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me,
verses.tsw_comparator: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me,

verses.rationale: Retains humiliating means and escape.
verses.before: but I was let down in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his hands.
verses.after: but I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: but I was let down in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his hands.

verses.rationale: Keeps necessity, lack of benefit, and topic shift.
verses.before: It is necessary to boast, though there is nothing to be gained. I will go on to visions and revelations of the Lord.
verses.after: I must boast. It is not beneficial, but I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is necessary to boast, though there is nothing to be gained. I will go on to visions and revelations of the Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves third-person restraint, exact time, uncertainty, and repetition.
verses.before: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago—whether in the body I do not know, or out of the body I do not know, God knows—was caught up to the third heaven.
verses.after: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven—whether in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know; God knows.
verses.tsw_comparator: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago—whether in the body I do not know, or out of the body I do not know, God knows—was caught up to the third heaven.

verses.rationale: Keeps the deliberate repeated uncertainty.
verses.before: I know that this man—whether in the body or apart from the body I do not know, God knows—
verses.after: And I know that this man—whether in the body or apart from the body I do not know; God knows—
verses.tsw_comparator: And I know that this man—whether in the body or apart from the body I do not know, God knows—

verses.rationale: Preserves paradise, unheard speech, and prohibition.
verses.before: was caught up into paradise and heard inexpressible words, which it is not permitted for a person to speak.
verses.after: was caught up into paradise and heard inexpressible words that a human is not permitted to speak.
verses.tsw_comparator: was caught up into paradise and heard inexpressible words, which it is not permitted for a person to speak.

verses.rationale: Keeps person distinction and exception.
verses.before: On behalf of such a one I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except in weaknesses.
verses.after: I will boast about such a person, but I will not boast about myself except in my weaknesses.
verses.tsw_comparator: On behalf of such a one I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except in weaknesses.

verses.rationale: Preserves restraint and evidence limit.
verses.before: For if I should wish to boast, I would not be foolish, for I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, so that no one may think more of me than what he sees in me or hears from me.
verses.after: For if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be speaking truth. But I refrain, so that no one will credit me with more than what is seen in me or heard from me,
verses.tsw_comparator: For if I should wish to boast, I would not be foolish, for I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, so that no one may think more of me than what he sees in me or hears from me.

verses.rationale: Keeps cause ambiguity, thorn, Satanic messenger, violence, and repetition.
verses.before: And because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations, therefore, so that I might not be exalted beyond measure, a thorn was given to me in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to strike me, so that I might not be exalted beyond measure.
verses.after: even because of the extraordinary revelations. Therefore, so that I would not become conceited, a thorn was given to me in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to strike me, so that I would not become conceited.
verses.tsw_comparator: And because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations, therefore, so that I might not be exalted beyond measure, a thorn was given to me in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to strike me, so that I might not be exalted beyond measure.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact count and request.
verses.before: Three times I pleaded with the Lord about this, that it should depart from me.
verses.after: Three times I pleaded with the Lord about this, that it would leave me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Three times I pleaded with the Lord about this, that it should depart from me.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct answer, paradox, and tenting image.
verses.before: And he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is brought to completion in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
verses.after: But he said to me, “My grace is enough for you, for power is brought to completion in weakness.” Therefore I will most gladly boast all the more in my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may dwell over me.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is brought to completion in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

verses.rationale: Retains real harms, reason, and paradox.
verses.before: So I am content with weaknesses, with insults, with hardships, with persecutions, and with distresses, for the sake of Christ. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
verses.after: Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and distress for Christ, for whenever I am weak, then I am strong.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I am content with weaknesses, with insults, with hardships, with persecutions, and with distresses, for the sake of Christ. For when I am weak, then I am strong.

verses.rationale: Keeps blame, expected defense, irony, and self-negation.
verses.before: I have become foolish—you compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you. For I was in no way inferior to the super-apostles, even if I am nothing.
verses.after: I have become a fool; you forced me to it. For I ought to have been recommended by you, because I was in no way inferior to the “super-apostles,” even though I am nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have become foolish—you compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you. For I was in no way inferior to the super-apostles, even if I am nothing.

verses.rationale: Preserves passive action, endurance, and three manifestations.
verses.before: The signs of an apostle were performed among you with all endurance, with signs and wonders and works of power.
verses.after: The signs of an apostle were performed among you with all endurance, by signs, wonders, and miracles.
verses.tsw_comparator: The signs of an apostle were performed among you with all endurance, with signs and wonders and works of power.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical comparison and biting apology.
verses.before: For in what were you treated as inferior to the other churches, except that I myself did not burden you? Forgive me this wrong.
verses.after: In what way were you treated as less than the other churches, except that I myself did not burden you? Forgive me this wrong!
verses.tsw_comparator: For in what were you treated as inferior to the other churches, except that I myself did not burden you? Forgive me this wrong.

verses.rationale: Preserves visit count, financial claim, and parental analogy.
verses.before: Here for the third time I am ready to come to you. And I will not be a burden, for I seek not what is yours but you. For children ought not to store up for the parents, but parents for the children.
verses.after: Look, I am ready to come to you this third time, and I will not burden you, because I seek not what you own, but you. For children should not save up for their parents, but parents for their children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Here for the third time I am ready to come to you. And I will not be a burden, for I seek not what is yours but you. For children ought not to store up for the parents, but parents for the children.

verses.rationale: Keeps financial/person metaphor and painful question.
verses.before: I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more, am I to be loved less?
verses.after: I will most gladly spend and be spent for your lives. If I love you more, am I to be loved less?
verses.tsw_comparator: I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more, am I to be loved less?

verses.rationale: Preserves voiced accusation as an ironic question.
verses.before: But be that as it may, I did not burden you. Yet, being crafty, I caught you by deceit.
verses.after: But let it be so: I did not burden you. Yet, being crafty, did I catch you by deceit?
verses.tsw_comparator: But be that as it may, I did not burden you. Yet, being crafty, I caught you by deceit.

verses.rationale: Keeps the direct challenge about intermediaries.
verses.before: Did I take advantage of you through any of those whom I sent to you?
verses.after: Did I exploit you through any of those I sent to you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Did I take advantage of you through any of those whom I sent to you?

verses.rationale: Preserves Titus, companion, questions, and shared conduct.
verses.before: I urged Titus to go, and I sent the brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not walk in the same steps?
verses.after: I urged Titus to go and sent the brother with him. Did Titus exploit you? Did we not walk in the same spirit and in the same footsteps?
verses.tsw_comparator: I urged Titus to go, and I sent the brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not walk in the same steps?

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical question, divine audience, affection, and purpose.
verses.before: Have you been thinking all along that we are defending ourselves to you? It is before God that we speak in Christ, and all for your building up, beloved.
verses.after: Have you been thinking all along that we are defending ourselves to you? We speak before God in Christ, and everything, beloved, is for building you up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you been thinking all along that we are defending ourselves to you? It is before God that we speak in Christ, and all for your building up, beloved.

verses.rationale: Preserves mutual disappointment and complete vice list.
verses.before: For I fear that perhaps when I come I may find you not as I wish, and that you may find me not as you wish—that perhaps there may be quarreling, jealousy, anger, rivalries, slander, gossip, conceit, disorder.
verses.after: For I fear that when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and you may not find me as you wish—that there may be strife, jealousy, fits of anger, selfish ambition, slander, gossip, conceit, and disorder.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I fear that perhaps when I come I may find you not as I wish, and that you may find me not as you wish—that perhaps there may be quarreling, jealousy, anger, rivalries, slander, gossip, conceit, disorder.

verses.rationale: Keeps fear, humiliation, grief, prior sin, and specific harms.
verses.before: I fear that when I come again my God may humble me before you, and I may mourn over many of people who have sinned before and have not repented of the impurity and sexual immorality and sensuality that they have practiced.
verses.after: I fear that when I come again, my God may humble me before you and I may mourn over many who sinned earlier and have not repented of the impurity, sexual immorality, and debauchery they practiced.
verses.tsw_comparator: I fear that when I come again my God may humble me before you, and I may mourn over many of those who have sinned before and have not repented of the impurity and sexual immorality and sensuality that they have practiced.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact visit count and legal quotation.
verses.before: This is the third time I am coming to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
verses.after: This will be my third visit to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the third time I am coming to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”

verses.rationale: Keeps audiences, past warning, and severe future resolve.
verses.before: I warned people who sinned before and all the others, and I warn them now while absent, as I did when present on my second visit: if I come again, I will not spare them—
verses.after: I warned those who sinned earlier and everyone else, and now I warn them in advance while absent, just as I did when present the second time: if I come again, I will not spare them,
verses.tsw_comparator: I warned those who sinned before and all the others, and I warn them now while absent, as I did when present on my second visit: if I come again, I will not spare them—

verses.rationale: Preserves requested proof and weakness/power contrast.
verses.before: since you are seeking proof that Christ is speaking in me. He is not weak toward you, but is powerful among you.
verses.after: since you seek proof that Christ is speaking in me. He is not weak toward you, but is powerful among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: since you are seeking proof that Christ is speaking in me. He is not weak toward you, but is powerful among you.

verses.rationale: Keeps crucifixion, life, and applied parallel.
verses.before: For he was crucified in weakness, but lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we will live with him by the power of God toward you.
verses.after: For he was crucified in weakness, yet he lives by God's power. For we too are weak in him, yet we will live with him by God's power in our dealings with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he was crucified in weakness, but lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we will live with him by the power of God toward you.

verses.rationale: Preserves reflexive commands and communal Christ relation.
verses.before: Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Or do you not recognize this about yourselves—that Jesus Christ is in you—unless indeed you fail the test?
verses.after: Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Or do you not recognize about yourselves that Jesus Christ is among you—unless, indeed, you fail the test?
verses.tsw_comparator: Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Or do you not recognize this about yourselves—that Jesus Christ is in you—unless indeed you fail the test?

verses.rationale: Keeps the hoped-for reciprocal recognition.
verses.before: Yet I hope that you will recognize that we have not failed the test.
verses.after: But I hope you will recognize that we have not failed the test.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I hope that you will recognize that we have not failed the test.

verses.rationale: Preserves ethical aim over apostolic reputation.
verses.before: Now we pray to God that you may not do wrong—not that we may appear approved, but that you may do what is right, even if we seem to have failed.
verses.after: Now we pray to God that you do nothing wrong—not so that we may appear to have passed the test, but so that you may do what is right, even if we appear to have failed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now we pray to God that you may not do wrong—not that we may appear approved, but that you may do what is right, even if we seem to have failed.

verses.rationale: Keeps absolute contrast and repeated truth.
verses.before: For we are not able to do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
verses.after: For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we are not able to do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.

verses.rationale: Preserves weakness/strength and concise goal.
verses.before: For we rejoice when we are weak and you are strong. Your restoration is what we pray for.
verses.after: For we rejoice whenever we are weak but you are strong. We also pray for this: your restoration.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we rejoice when we are weak and you are strong. Your restoration is what we pray for.

verses.rationale: Keeps absence/presence, severity, authority, and its limit.
verses.before: For this reason I write these things while absent, so that when present I may not have to act severely, according to the authority that the Lord gave me for building up and not for tearing down.
